nextGame.note: Sunday home game in the Superdome against Cleveland. It was today at noon, and the Saints won 23-22 in overtime. They were behind 13-9 with a minute to go, scored to take the lead, gave up a tying field goal with eight seconds left, then won it in overtime.

news.headline: Saints beat Cleveland 23-22 in overtime
news.summary: Tyler Shough threw a 15-yard touchdown to Juwan Johnson in overtime, and the Saints held on when Cleveland scored at the very end but missed its two-point try. It is the Saints' first home win of the season, and they are now three wins and five losses.

news.headline: Alvin Kamara is set to play Sunday
news.summary: Kamara practiced in full on Friday and the Saints gave him no injury designation for the Cleveland game, after he rested his back on Wednesday. Running back C.J. Donaldson is out with a shoulder injury and a concussion, and rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson is questionable for what would be his first NFL game.

news.headline: Cleveland rules out Deshaun Watson for Sunday
news.summary: Browns coach Todd Monken said Friday that his quarterback will not play in the Superdome because of a concussion. Rookie Shedeur Sanders will start against the Saints instead.

nextGame.note: Saturday evening road game in Lexington, Kentucky. A quarter past five our time. Florida has won five games and lost four and needs one more win to reach a bowl game.

news.headline: Oklahoma beats Florida 23-7 in Gainesville
news.summary: Florida scored one touchdown, in the second quarter, and did not score again. The Gators have lost four of their last five games and are five wins and four losses.

news.headline: Sumrall explains the fourth-down call that went wrong
news.summary: Behind 13-7 late in the third quarter, Florida passed up a short field goal and threw on fourth down from the Oklahoma 17. Oklahoma caught the ball instead, and Coach Jon Sumrall said afterward his offense simply did not play well enough to win.

news.headline: Florida plans to start Tramell Jones at quarterback
news.summary: ESPN reported Thursday that Jones will start Saturday night against Oklahoma instead of Aaron Philo. Florida has not announced it, and Philo was pulled from the Georgia game after two interceptions.

nextGame.note: Saturday night home game in Baton Rouge. Half past six our time. LSU has won six games and lost three. Texas has won seven and lost two.

news.headline: Alabama beats LSU 31-13 in Tiger Stadium
news.summary: Sam Leavitt threw for 380 yards, but LSU missed on all four of its fourth-down tries and scored only 13 points. The Tigers are now six wins and three losses.

news.headline: Whit Weeks is now expected to miss the Alabama game
news.summary: A CBS Sports reporter said Thursday that LSU does not expect its best linebacker to play Saturday. He broke a bone in his leg in late September, and the team had hoped he would be ready for this one.

news.headline: Princewill Umanmielen is up for a national award
news.summary: LSU's defensive end is one of 12 players still in the running for the Lombardi Award, which goes to the best lineman or linebacker in the country. Four finalists are named November 18 and the winner on December 9.

nextGame.note: Saturday afternoon road game in Houston. One o'clock our time. Tulane has won four games and lost five. Rice has won four games and lost five too. Tulane needs two more wins to reach a bowl game.

news.headline: Tulsa routs Tulane 60-10 at Homecoming
news.summary: Tulsa led 32-0 at halftime and Tulane never got going, losing by 50 points in front of the Homecoming crowd at Yulman Stadium. It is the worst conference loss Tulane has ever had, and the Green Wave are now four wins and five losses.

news.headline: Tulane's athletic director calls the loss unacceptable
news.summary: David Harris, who runs sports at Tulane, put out a statement Saturday night saying he was embarrassed and that losing by 50 points was unacceptable. He did not announce any changes to the coaching staff.

news.headline: Tulane punter William Hudlow is up for a national award
news.summary: Hudlow is one of 65 players nominated for the Burlsworth Trophy, which goes to the best player who started college without a scholarship. He averages 47 yards a punt, the best in his conference.
